metadata.title: TALIS 2018 Results (Volume I): Teachers and School Leaders as Lifelong Learners

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD TALIS 2018 volume reports results from a complex, multi-stage sample of schools and teachers/principals across participating countries and economies, with target response rates specified for both school and respondent levels. The reader’s guide states that principal responses are usually weighted by school weights, and in cases where principals’ answers are treated as teacher-level attributes, they are weighted by teacher weights—indicating the use of sampling weights for representative estimation. The publication does not provide the exact weight variable names in the excerpt, nor does it describe replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so replicate-weight usage cannot be confirmed from the provided text. The report also emphasizes that TALIS results are based on self-reports and that no data imputation from administrative data or other studies is conducted; missing or non-reported estimates are denoted with symbols (e.g., a, c, p, w) rather than imputed.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because TALIS is a questionnaire-based survey of teachers and school leaders (attitudes, practices, perceptions) rather than a cognitive achievement assessment that generates PV-based scale scores. Missing data handling is not reported in the provided text because the report instead uses adjudication and reporting symbols (e.g., a, c, p, w) to indicate when items were not administered, too few observations existed, or data were removed/withheld for technical reasons. This indicates that the publication focuses on reporting availability and confidentiality constraints rather than documenting a specific statistical missing-data imputation procedure.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used TALIS 2018 survey data covering lower secondary education (ISCED 2) as the main target population, with additional options for ISCED 1 (primary) and ISCED 3 (upper secondary) and a TALIS-PISA link option for some countries. The sampling design targets 200 schools per country and 20 teachers plus 1 school leader per school, with response-rate criteria defining whether a school is considered to have responded (50% of sampled teachers respond) and target response rates for teachers and school leaders. The publication also applies adjudication rules for teacher, school, and principal data and excludes or withholds estimates when participation rates are below standards or when confidentiality thresholds are not met (e.g., fewer than 10 schools/principals or 30 teachers with valid data, or item non-response above 50%).

data.outcome_summary: This OECD TALIS 2018 Results (Volume I) report synthesizes questionnaire-based evidence from teachers and school leaders about teaching practices, assessment practices, classroom time use, school climate, professional development, and teacher professionalism. The survey targets lower secondary education (ISCED 2) as the main population, with additional country options for ISCED 1 and ISCED 3 and a TALIS-PISA link for some participating systems. The design is cross-sectional and explicitly based on self-reports, so it cannot measure causality; the report also cautions that trends across cycles require careful interpretation because the set of participating countries/economies changes over time. Results are presented as international comparisons and trends, with international averages computed as arithmetic means (or EU totals as weighted averages) across participating countries meeting adjudication standards. The excerpt does not describe any machine-learning model training or predictive performance metrics; instead, it provides descriptive benchmarking and statistically significant differences/changes as denoted in figures and tables.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD TALIS 2018 results volume that reports survey findings and policy implications rather than an empirical machine-learning study with a defined predictive target, model training, and reported ML performance metrics. As a result, fields such as total_students, per-country student counts, PV handling, missing-data imputation strategy, and ML techniques are not available in the provided text excerpt. The report’s methodological emphasis is on survey design, adjudication, weighting at the school/teacher/principal level, and reporting conventions for non-reported estimates rather than on ML-based prediction.
